title: Optimized pipeline for isolation and analysis of live single cells
author: Yaron, Ziegler, et al.
materials: Terasaki-style microtest plates (#470378, Thermo Scientific, Pittsburgh, PA) were briefly cleaned using pressurized nitrogen gas to remove particulate from the well area. The plates were then exposed to air plasma in a plasma cleaner (PDC-001, Harrick Plasma, Ithaca, NY) for 1 minute under 500 mTorr vacuum with 10.15 W RF-power; we noticed a decrease in the time necessary for cell spreading after plasma treating, but this step is not required. The outer surfaces of the plates were sprayed with 70% ethanol and allowed to dry in a sterile, laminar flow hood prior to cell seeding.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension
steps.instruction: Maintain CP-A, CP-D, THP-1, and MDA-MB-231 cells in their respective media (serum‑free Keratinocyte medium with 20 ng/mL EGF, 140 µg/mL bovine pituitary extract, 100 U/mL penicillin, 100 µg/mL streptomycin; or DMEM with 10 % FBS, 100 U/mL penicillin, 100 µg/mL streptomycin) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Detach adherent cells with 0.05 % Trypsin‑EDTA for 10 min, centrifuge at 900 rpm for 3 min, count using Trypan Blue on a Countess® counter and retain only preparations ≥95 % viable. Resuspend cells at 200–300 cells/mL (or 1:1 mixture if specified).

steps.title: Prepare Terasaki plates
steps.instruction: Clean Terasaki‑style microtest plates (#470378, Thermo Scientific) with pressurized nitrogen gas to remove particulates. Optionally treat the well surfaces with air plasma for 1 min under 500 mTorr vacuum at 10.15 W RF‑power (improves spreading for weakly adherent lines). Spray outer surfaces with 70 % ethanol and let dry in a sterile laminar‑flow hood before seeding.

steps.title: Generate calibration curve
steps.instruction: Prepare cell suspensions ranging from 50 to 500 cells/mL in 50‑cell increments. Seed each concentration into Terasaki plates as described below, then manually count wells to determine occupancy distribution for each density.

steps.title: Seed cells for single occupancy
steps.instruction: Using the optimal density of 200–300 cells/mL, add the cell suspension to the prepared Terasaki plates. Allow cells to settle, then count wells; typically 15–25 wells per plate contain a single live cell, matching Poisson expectations (R² > 0.98).

steps.title: Incubate and apply treatments
steps.instruction: Perform the following actions in order:

substeps.instruction: Transfer the plate to an incubator or keep in a cell‑culture hood for a minimum of 10–20 minutes.
(Optional) Incubate overnight or as needed for full adhesion.
(Optional) Add drugs or other experimental treatments.
(Optional) Stain cells with vital dyes or fluorescent indicators.

steps.title: Image live single cells
steps.instruction: Acquire bright‑field or fluorescence images of each well containing a single live cell to record morphology and any physiological indicators.

steps.title: Harvest cells for RNA
steps.instruction: Collect individual wells with single cells, place them at –80 °C (storage < 1 week) until RNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract total RNA
steps.instruction: Using the Quick‑RNA™ MicroPrep kit, follow these steps:

substeps.instruction: Transfer lysate to a Zymo‑Spin™ IC column in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Add 400 µL RNA Pre‑Wash Buffer, centrifuge 12,000 × g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Add 700 µL RNA Wash Buffer, centrifuge 12,000 × g for 1 min; discard flow‑through. Repeat with 400 µL RNA Wash Buffer.
Centrifuge the column with the empty collection tube at 12,000 × g for 2 min to remove residual buffer.

Place the column in an RNase/DNase‑free 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 9 µL DEPC‑treated water, let sit 1 min, then centrifuge 12,000 × g for 1 min. Eluted total RNA (9 µL) can be used immediately or stored at ≤ –80 °C.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Perform first‑strand cDNA synthesis in a thermal cycler (Life Technologies) using the eluted RNA (9 µL) under the cycling conditions described in the detailed protocol; store resulting cDNA at –20 °C until further use.
